<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

See six things you can build while patient rows stay on the server, then choose
the chapter that teaches your next step.
</div>

Read the cards as a quick tour, or run them in order. Each output is a real
2.10.4 result. The first four cards use the **24-person synthetic questionnaire
fixture**, not APHRC patient data; the last two use **synthetic Synthea27Nj labs**.

**You need:** the packages and downloaded helpers from
[Before you start](book-00-start.html#before-you-start). Start a fresh R session
in `book-work`. The local fixture makes the vocabulary comparison reproducible.


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture(two_sites = TRUE)
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
```

```
#> [1] "site"  "site2"
```

The two sites have the same synthetic answer patterns but different vocabulary
wording. They illustrate harmonisation, not two independent study populations.

<div class="capability-card">

## Named concepts across sites

**One categorical column, shared meanings.** Declare a common label for the
same education concept, then ask each site for a protected count table.


``` r
named <- omop_recipe(variables = list(education = omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", 900001L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"),
  labels = c("900102" = "University education"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(named, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
recipe_execute(named, out = c(people = "D_tour_named"), conns = conns)
named_tables <- lapply(names(conns), function(site)
  ds.omop.table("D_tour_named", "education", conns = conns[site]))
names(named_tables) <- names(conns)
named_tables
```

```
#> $site
#> D_tour_named$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6 
#> 
#> $site2
#> D_tour_named$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6
```

The same labels appear at both sites even though their local names differ.
These are released counts, not an export of education answers.
[Learn concepts and harmonisation →](book-10-harmonise.html)

</div>

Use one site for the next three cards; keep the other connection for cleanup.


``` r
two_conns <- conns
conns <- two_conns[1L]
names(conns)
```

<div class="capability-card">

## Dates in your study's format, and completed ages

**Separate a date's meaning from its presentation.** This recipe uses a custom
month-year pattern and completed birthdays at death.


``` r
dates <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  month = omop_date("first_visit", omop_date_spec(precision = "custom",
    pattern = "%b %Y")), age = omop_age_at("death")),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(dates, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
recipe_execute(dates, out = c(people = "D_tour_dates"), conns = conns)
ds.omop.table("D_tour_dates", "month", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_tour_dates$month
#> Mar 2020 Jun 2020 Jul 2020 
#>        6        6        6
```


``` r
age_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_tour_dates$age", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(age_result))
```



|Site |Statistic | Value|
|:----|:---------|-----:|
|site |5%        |    33|
|site |10%       |    33|
|site |25%       |    33|
|site |50%       |    38|
|site |75%       |    43|
|site |90%       |    43|
|site |95%       |    43|
|site |Mean      |    38|

Complete birth/death records give ages 33 and 43. Missing dates stay missing.
Exact dates, numeric periods, month/quarter/year categories, date parts and
supported custom patterns serve different questions; category release rules
still apply. [Learn dates and ages →](book-09-dates.html)

</div>

<div class="capability-card">

## Choose the output shape

**Person → event → period → follow-up.** Wide tables support named covariates;
long tables retain events; panels repeat time bins; survival records end at an
outcome or declared censor. All four remain private server tables.


``` r
visits <- omop_event("visit_occurrence", c(9201L, 9202L), name = "visits")
visitors <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visits))
base <- omop_recipe(events = list(visits), populations = list(visitors),
  variables = list(visits = omop_variable(event = visits, reducer = omop_reduce("count"))),
  outputs = omop_output("wide", rows = "visitors", format = "wide"))
shapes <- list(
  wide = base$outputs[[1L]],
  long = omop_output("long", rows = "visitors", format = "long", sources = "visits"),
  panel = omop_output("panel", rows = "visitors", format = "person_period",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), bins = list(width = 30L),
      window = omop_window(1, 90), analyses = "count")),
  survival = omop_output("survival", rows = "visitors", format = "survival",
    options = list(outcomes = list(revisit = visits), tar = omop_window(1, 365),
      censor = list("observation_end", "death"))))
```

The same population enters at its first visit. The panel has three 30-day bins;
survival asks about the first repeat visit within a year, stopping earlier at
observation end or death.


``` r
shape_columns <- lapply(names(shapes), function(shape) {
  recipe <- base
  recipe$outputs <- setNames(list(shapes[[shape]]), shape)
  stopifnot(recipe_explain(recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
  target <- paste0("D_tour_", shape)
  recipe_execute(recipe, out = setNames(target, shape), conns = conns)
  columns <- dsBaseClient::ds.colnames(target, datasources = conns)[[1L]]
  data.frame(Shape = shape, Columns = paste(columns, collapse = ", "))
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, shape_columns))
```



|Shape    |Columns                                                                                                                                 |
|:--------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|wide     |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, visits                                                                                                |
|long     |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, concept_id, start_date, end_date, visit_type_concept_id                                               |
|panel    |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, period_start_days, period_end_days, days, visits_inpatient_visit_count, visits_outpatient_visit_count |
|survival |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, outcome_name, event, entry_days_from_index, exit_days_from_index, follow_up_days                      |

These are actual released column inventories, not patient rows. Panels and long
tables contain repeated observations, so row count is not independent sample size.

<details><summary>More shapes: presets, intervals, sparse data and joins</summary>

Features and baseline are wide presets. Temporal covariates add time indices to
sparse values; intervals retain bounds; membership retains population episodes;
a dictionary describes concepts; joined combines declared private dependencies.
The following executes each additional form on the same small study.


``` r
more <- list(
  features = omop_output("features", rows = "visitors", type = "features"),
  baseline = omop_output("baseline", rows = "visitors", type = "baseline"),
  intervals = omop_output("intervals", rows = "visitors", format = "intervals",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), window = omop_window(0, NULL))),
  sparse = omop_output("sparse", rows = "visitors", format = "sparse",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), analyses = "count")),
  temporal = omop_output("temporal", rows = "visitors", format = "temporal_covariates",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), bin_width = 30L,
      window = omop_window(0, 89), analyses = "count")),
  membership = omop_output("membership", rows = "visitors", format = "membership"))
more_columns <- lapply(names(more), function(shape) {
  recipe <- base
  recipe$outputs <- setNames(list(more[[shape]]), shape)
  stopifnot(recipe_explain(recipe, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
  target <- paste0("D_tour_", shape)
  recipe_execute(recipe, out = setNames(target, shape), conns = conns)
  data.frame(Shape = shape, Columns = paste(
    dsBaseClient::ds.colnames(target, datasources = conns)[[1L]], collapse = ", "))
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, more_columns))
```



|Shape      |Columns                                                                                                 |
|:----------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|features   |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, visits                                                                |
|baseline   |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, visits                                                                |
|intervals  |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, interval_type, concept_id, start_days_from_index, end_days_from_index |
|sparse     |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, covariate_id, covariate_value                                         |
|temporal   |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, time_id, covariate_id, covariate_value                                |
|membership |row_id, cohort_row_id, person_id, cohort_start_date, cohort_end_date, index_source                      |

Sparse outputs also create reference companions that define their numeric keys.
Keep those companions for interpretation.


``` r
dictionary <- base
dictionary$outputs$dictionary <- omop_output("dictionary", rows = "visitors",
  format = "dictionary", options = list(source_outputs = "wide"))
dictionary$publish <- "dictionary"
stopifnot(recipe_explain(dictionary, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
recipe_execute(dictionary, out = c(dictionary = "D_tour_dictionary"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_tour_dictionary", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> [1] "concept_id"       "concept_name"     "domain_id"        "vocabulary_id"   
#> [5] "concept_class_id" "source"
```

``` r
joined <- base
joined$variables$age <- omop_age_at("first_visit")
joined$outputs <- list(
  counts = omop_output("counts", rows = "visitors", format = "wide", columns = "visits"),
  ages = omop_output("ages", rows = "visitors", format = "wide", columns = "age"),
  joined = omop_output("joined", rows = "visitors", format = "joined",
    options = list(from = list(list(output = "counts"), list(output = "ages")),
      how = "left", cardinality = "one_to_one")))
joined$publish <- "joined"
stopifnot(recipe_explain(joined, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
recipe_execute(joined, out = c(joined = "D_tour_joined"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_tour_joined", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> [1] "row_id"        "cohort_row_id" "person_id"     "visits"        "age"
```

The join adds an age column without multiplying episodes. Only the dictionary
or joined result is published in those respective calls.

</details>

[Learn every output format →](book-08-outputs.html)
[Then analyse longitudinal data →](book-16-longitudinal.html)

</div>

## The APHRC colleague's verbal-autopsy table

**One wide table combines the study variables.** The downloadable helper builds
the released recipe: pseudonymous person key, completed ages, education and fever
answers, visit periods, dates and coded cause of death.


``` r
source("tools/dates/va-native.R")
va <- va_native_recipe()
stopifnot(recipe_explain(va, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
recipe_execute(va, out = c(people = "D_tour_va"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_tour_va", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#>  [1] "person_id"          "age_at_death"       "age_at_first_visit" "education"         
#>  [5] "fever"              "visit_date"         "visit_month"        "visit_quarter"     
#>  [9] "visit_year"         "visit_parts_year"   "visit_parts_month"  "death_date"        
#> [13] "cause_of_death"
```

``` r
ds.omop.table("D_tour_va", "cause_of_death", conns = conns)
```

```
#> D_tour_va$cause_of_death
#> Myocardial infarction             Pneumonia 
#>                    12                     6
```

The cause counts are synthetic questionnaire-fixture results, not APHRC findings.
The person key and patient rows stay private; education and cause are each one
named categorical column in the same table.
[Build this table step by step →](book-18-verbal-autopsy.html)

<div class="capability-card">

## Numbers and their groupings

**Keep the number and a declared band.** Reduce hemoglobin to one mean per
person, in recorded g/dL, and group those means using public teaching breaks.


``` r
labs <- omop_recipe(variables = list(hb = omop_mean_value("measurement", 3000963L,
  unit = 8713L, window = omop_window(NULL, NULL))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(labs, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
recipe_execute(labs, out = c(people = "D_tour_labs"), conns = conns)
ds.omop.mutate("D_tour_labs", band = cut(hb, c(0, 14, 15, 100),
  labels = c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above"), right = FALSE),
  newobj = "D_tour_bands", conns = conns)
band_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_tour_bands$band", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
mean_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_tour_bands$hb", type = "combine", datasources = conns)
band_display <- book_group_comparison(band_result, mean_result, "Person mean hemoglobin", "g/dL")
band_display$Category <- ordered(band_display$Category,
  levels = c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above"))
knitr::kable(band_display[order(band_display$Category), c("Category", "Count", "Mean")],
  row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Band (g/dL)", "People", "Mean (g/dL)"))
```



|Band (g/dL)    | People| Mean (g/dL)|
|:--------------|------:|-----------:|
|below 14       |      9|    14.46679|
|14 to below 15 |      9|    14.46679|
|15 or above    |     10|    14.46679|

Counts 9, 9 and 10 cover all 28 people. The repeated numeric mean is the overall
mean of person means, not a mean within each band. Only the released display
labels are ordered here. The breaks are teaching choices, not clinical ranges.
[Learn reducers, units, flags and pooled analysis →](book-14-labs.html)

</div>

<div class="capability-card">

## Derive and filter without downloading rows

**Add a column, then select with a condition.** The closed mutate-v1 grammar
supports arithmetic; `omop_where` declares the filter predicate.


``` r
ds.omop.mutate("D_tour_labs", hb_gl = hb * 10,
  newobj = "D_tour_converted", conns = conns)
ds.omop.filter("D_tour_converted", expr = omop_where(hb >= 14),
  newobj = "D_tour_selected", conns = conns)
selected_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_tour_selected$hb_gl", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(selected_result))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value|
|:----|:---------|--------:|
|site |5%        | 140.9333|
|site |10%       | 141.0533|
|site |25%       | 143.2500|
|site |50%       | 151.2500|
|site |75%       | 155.7917|
|site |90%       | 158.9000|
|site |95%       | 159.9500|
|site |Mean      | 149.9991|

The retained people's values are expressed in g/L, ten times g/dL. The final
subset passes its publication check; the analyst receives only this summary.
[Learn BMI, age groups, recodes and rollback →](book-11-parameters.html)

</div>

## Recap

Select concepts, choose time and units, request the table shape, and derive
columns privately. DataSHIELD returns approved summaries while rows stay at sites.

## Try it

Use the converted table to summarise all people, without the filter. Why does
the mean differ from the preceding card?

<details><summary>Solution</summary>


``` r
all_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_tour_converted$hb_gl", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_summary(all_result))
```



|Site |Statistic |    Value|
|:----|:---------|--------:|
|site |5%        | 129.0500|
|site |10%       | 131.4667|
|site |25%       | 137.8500|
|site |50%       | 143.2500|
|site |75%       | 153.3542|
|site |90%       | 157.0000|
|site |95%       | 159.2375|
|site |Mean      | 144.6679|

This mean is 144.667857 g/L, ten times the earlier all-person mean in g/dL.
The filtered card excludes people whose person mean is below 14 g/dL, so its
mean is higher. The unit conversion alone does not select people.

</details>
